thread:
josh: Customer tenant reports svc endpoint svc.acme.internal returning NXDOMAIN from their VPC after we migrated the private hosted zone to the shared account during onboarding. Impacting production traffic, customer asks for urgent help.

anika: on it — can you paste the VPC id and a dig from an affected host?

josh: VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d (acct 123456789012). Here is the dig they ran from an EC2 instance: 

```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc.acme.internal @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
acme.internal. 300 IN SOA ns-123.awsdns-45.net.
```

devon: NXDOMAIN from VPC resolver generally means the private hosted zone that's supposed to serve the name isn't associated with that VPC or there's a shadowing private zone in the same VPC. This happened right after the hosted-zone move — likely missing VPC association. Can you confirm hosted zone id and owner?

josh: Control-plane shows hosted zone Z-SHARED-1 in account shared-account (owner), but associations list does NOT include vpc-0a1b2c3d. Customer's account shows an empty acme.internal private zone Z-LOCAL-XXX (few records) that does NOT contain the svc record.

maggie-sre: that matches — move created the zone in shared-account but the VPC association was never created for the tenant VPC. For cross-account association you must call associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone from the hosted-zone owner account.

anika: steps: (1) confirm hosted-zone owner will associate vpc-0a1b2c3d, (2) after association ask customer to flush resolver caches and test again. Also check if they have any custom resolver rules forwarding to on-prem which could shadow responses.

josh: asked customer to run describe-vpc and check DNS settings — they confirmed "enableDnsSupport" and "enableDnsHostnames" are true. They also showed /etc/resolv.conf pointing to 10.0.0.2 (VPC resolver) then 172.16.0.2 (on-prem VPN).

devon: good. Owner account should run: 

```
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z-SHARED-1 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d --comment "associate for tenant handover"
```

josh: Owner performed association (change-id CH12345). Immediately after association, customer still hit NXDOMAIN.

anika: likely stale cache — many hosts run node-local dns caching (169.254.20.10) or systemd-resolved. Ask them to restart the node-local resolver or flush cache and re-run dig directly to VPC resolver: `dig @10.0.0.2 svc.acme.internal +short`.

josh: customer restarted node-local resolver and retried. Dig now returns a CNAME -> svc-prod-1234.r-inference.internal and then A records. However their app now fails TLS handshake: `certificate verify failed: Hostname mismatch`.

devon: that indicates DNS now points to a target whose certificate CN/SAN does not include svc.acme.internal. We need to inspect the cert presented by the endpoint. Ask for `curl -vk https://svc.acme.internal/` output or openssl s_client.

josh: pasted curl -vk results: server certificate CN = svc-prod-1234.r-inference.internal, SANs do not include svc.acme.internal. Client rejects SNI.

maggie-sre: two potential root causes: (A) DNS record is a CNAME to an internal hostname that presents a different cert (common if record points to internal ALB/privatelink target), or (B) during migration the record was recreated incorrectly (pointing to a generic shared target).

anika: remediation options: (1) update DNS to point to an alias/record that matches the cert (if the client can use that hostname), (2) request ACM to issue a cert that covers svc.acme.internal for that backend, or (3) change client SNI to match backend (not ideal). Short-term, association + cache flush + correct record needed.

josh: we've opened infra ticket infra-ticket-789 to either update the target record or provision a cert for svc.acme.internal. Also advised customer to validate certificate after DNS change with: 

```
openssl s_client -connect <endpoint-ip>:443 -servername svc.acme.internal -showcerts
```

devon: added a small smoke-test snippet to the runbook (for future hosted-zone moves): 

```
# quick check after cross-account hosted-zone move
dig @10.0.0.2 svc.acme.internal +nocookie +time=2
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z-SHARED-1
aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id Z-SHARED-1
openssl s_client -connect $(dig +short svc.acme.internal | head -n1):443 -servername svc.acme.internal -brief
```

anika: also add an automated post-migration check: verify VPC associations for all affected tenant VPCs and run resolution + cert checks from a small fleet of probes in each region. Will file a follow-up to add to the migration playbook.

josh: customer confirmed service recovered after we updated the DNS target and provisioned a cert that included svc.acme.internal. They'll keep an eye on it for 24h. Closing the escalation and adding notes to the runbook. Thanks all! :party-parrot:

sre-bot: incident-closed | 3467890123 | severity: high | summary: private-dns NXDOMAIN -> assoc+cache+cert fix applied
